metadata.title: CGE-P Capstone — Patient Intake API component definition

components.title: Patient Intake API
components.description: Governed Patient Intake API: HTTP API Gateway in front of a VPC-attached Lambda that writes intake records to DynamoDB and objects to an S3 uploads bucket. Layer 1 Terraform closes the eight starter gaps; Layer 2 Rego blocks regressions at pull request; Layer 3 signs and vaults the evidence bundle this component links to.

control-implementations.description: NIST SP 800-171 Rev 3 requirements implemented by the Patient Intake API Terraform and, where the suite actually inspects them, enforced by the cgep.* Conftest packages. CMMC Level 2 practice IDs are carried as cmmc-practice props. Exactly eight implemented-requirements — AU.L2-3.3.1 spans 03.03.01 and 03.03.03. At-rest storage confidentiality is asserted on SP_800_171_03.13.08 alongside its transmission control (shared uploads CMK resources). Evidence link hrefs use the literal host segment EVIDENCE_BUCKET: the real bucket name is withheld per R-1 and resolves via `terraform -chdir=terraform output -raw evidence_bucket`.

implemented-requirements.description: Least privilege on the intake Lambda's inline policy (aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_inline): only dynamodb:PutItem on the intake table, s3:PutObject on the uploads object prefix, and sqs:SendMessage on the DLQ. That scoped claim does not extend to the three AWS managed policy attachments on the same role (AWSLambdaBasicExecutionRole, AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole, AWSXRayDaemonWriteAccess), which grant Resource "*" as AWS documents them. cgep.ac_3_01_05 checks Action wildcards only and ignores Resource — set all three Resource values to "*" and the gate stays green — so resource scoping is Terraform-only, unpoliced.

implemented-requirements.description: Event selection for the intake path: API Gateway HTTP API access logging to a dedicated CloudWatch log group (request id, source IP, route, status) plus a multi-region CloudTrail that captures management events. WAF is not attached — HTTP APIs do not support AWS WAF association in this account/API type, so throttling on the stage is the boundary control instead. cgep.au_3_03_01 carries two deny rules and enforces both halves of the API Gateway control, access logging and stage throttling; CloudTrail event selection is Terraform-configured and unpoliced by the suite.

implemented-requirements.description: Audit record generation: CloudTrail writes management-event records to a dedicated trail bucket with enable_log_file_validation set so delivered digests can detect tampering. This is the record-generation half of AU.L2-3.3.1; event selection is asserted under SP_800_171_03.03.01. The cited package cgep.au_3_03_01 only matches aws_apigatewayv2_stage, so it cannot deny a missing or unvalidated CloudTrail; record generation is Terraform-only and unpoliced.

implemented-requirements.description: System Backup – Cryptographic Protection on the uploads bucket: versioning Enabled produces recoverable object copies (prior versions after overwrite or delete), and the bucket CMK (workload customer-managed key via SSE-KMS) protects the confidentiality of those backup copies. Versioning alone would not satisfy this requirement — both halves are required. cgep.mp_3_08_09 covers the versioning half only (versioning_configuration.status); the CMK half is policed by a different package, cgep.sc_3_13_11, whose GAP-01 deny fires if the uploads bucket leaves SSE-KMS under a customer CMK.

implemented-requirements.description: Boundary protection: the intake Lambda runs with vpc_config in private subnets behind a security group that permits egress only to the S3 and DynamoDB gateway endpoint prefix lists and VPC DNS. Private route table has no internet route; gateway endpoints provide AWS API reachability without NAT. cgep.sc_3_13_01 asserts non-empty vpc_config subnet_ids and security_group_ids lists only; subnet identity, SG egress rules, and route-table content are Terraform-only, unpoliced.

implemented-requirements.description: Transmission and storage confidentiality for the uploads bucket: a bucket policy Deny rejects any S3 request where aws:SecureTransport is false, and the same bucket is encrypted at rest under the workload CMK via SSE-KMS. Rev 3 homes both halves here rather than on a related-requirement under 03.13.11. cgep.sc_3_13_08 covers the transmission (SecureTransport) half; the at-rest half is policed by a different package, cgep.sc_3_13_11, whose GAP-01 deny fires if the uploads bucket leaves SSE-KMS under a customer CMK. Both halves are gate-backed.

implemented-requirements.description: Cryptographic protection via two customer-managed KMS keys: the workload CMK (uploads bucket SSE-KMS and DynamoDB table encryption) and the evidence CMK (evidence vault SSE-KMS, trail bucket SSE-KMS, and CloudTrail kms_key_id so log objects are not overridden to AES256). cgep.sc_3_13_11 enforces only the uploads-bucket SSE-KMS rule and DynamoDB CMK encryption — Decision 43 scopes deny #1 to the uploads label. Evidence-vault SSE-KMS, trail-bucket SSE-KMS, and CloudTrail kms_key_id are Terraform-configured and unpoliced; removing the trail kms_key_id would leave the gate green.

implemented-requirements.description: System monitoring resources on the intake Lambda: a CMK-encrypted SQS dead-letter queue is attached via dead_letter_config, and Active X-Ray tracing is enabled. Reserved concurrency is not configured — account quota blocks it. The DLQ does not receive failed intake requests under the current trigger: API Gateway HTTP API AWS_PROXY invokes the function synchronously, and Lambda only delivers to DeadLetterConfig on asynchronous invocation. The queue closes GAP-06 as configured infrastructure; runtime routing of failed POSTs is inert until an async producer exists. cgep.si_3_14_06's has_dlq is the bare-reference form fn.values.dead_letter_config[_] — it binds on [{}] and on [{"target_arn": ""}] — so a non-empty but empty-ARN list keeps the gate green (same limitation named O5 in WRITEUP.md).
